title: Release 0.10.0: three of the six unreleased commits change behaviour a consumer can be broken by
body:
## Summary

`v0.9.0` is tagged at `f345ad7` and `package.json` still reads `0.9.0`, so this is a bump-then-tag release rather than the tag-only kind. Six commits have landed since:

| Commit | Issues | Consumer impact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `2f77e76` | #223 | Integration suite authenticates with client credentials |
| `2002dab` | #224, #226 | Integration suite fails rather than passing on mocks |
| `1daa7fb` | #227, #228 | **A failed lookup throws** where it returned empty; a token is asked of the named instance |
| `d36676e` | #231, #234, #235 | **Half a credential is refused** instead of falling through to route credentials |
| `cb015fe` | #208 | Integration suite gains a fixture it can fail against |
| `e459b3e` | #236, #238, #239, #240 | **Ambient Basic auth removed**; `getAssetListsPage` throws; site readers take an ERC |

## Resolution analysis: why 0.10.0 and not 0.9.1

Three of the six change behaviour a working consumer can be broken by, and one of them cannot be taken without an environment change:

1. **#236 requires action before the bump is safe.** A deployment that relied on `LIFERAY_API_USERNAME`/`LIFERAY_API_PASSWORD` being read whenever no `clientId` was present must now set `LIFERAY_AUTH_METHOD=basic`. Without it the call fails closed with `Liferay authentication is not configured`. That is the point of the fix, and it is precisely the thing a patch number promises is absent.
2. **#234/#235 turn a silent fallthrough into a 400.** A caller supplying one half of a credential pair used to get a token for this environment's own OAuth application; it now gets an error naming the missing half.
3. **#227/#228 turn a swallowed lookup failure into a throw.** A caller relying on the empty-collection behaviour sees an exception instead.

The argument for a patch is the same one #221 rejected for 0.9.0: the SDK has one consumer, pinned by tag, and nothing breaks in practice. But the version number is read by whoever comes next deciding whether a bump is safe to take, and a patch tells them nothing here can hurt them. This one can, for three reasons.

The remaining three commits touch only `tests/integration/` and the scripts that feed it, so they carry no runtime change at all.

## Implementation plan

1. Branch `chore/release-0.10.0`; bump `package.json` to `0.10.0`. Nothing else encodes the version - `tests/version.test.js` reads it from the package and asserts the exported value matches.
2. Run the gates: `yarn test`, `yarn lint`, `yarn validate`.
3. Open the bump PR closing this issue, and **stop there** for a human merge.
4. After the merge: annotated tag `v0.10.0` on the merge commit, then a GitHub release whose notes lead with the `LIFERAY_AUTH_METHOD=basic` migration.

There is no registry publish - no `publishConfig`, no publish workflow, and the README pins consumers by git tag. If a tarball is ever wanted, pack with **npm**, never `yarn pack`.

## Not in this release

Four items were recorded against #242 and remain open: the missing `account-group` key in `_getExclusions`' `keyMap`; `harvestInlinePaths` matching `/o/` paths in doc comments; the four remaining `KNOWN_UNVERIFIED_INLINE` entries #240 asks to re-check live; and the absent `*Page` variants for `getAccounts`/`getAccountGroups` (LDM #101).
